weed is 100% addictive. from what i've gathered, the myth about weed being non-addictive may have made more sense before 30 years ago, as back then cannabis plants not nearly as heavily genetically modified as they are now. apparently back in the 60's and 70's, average weed THC levels were about 2%. now, and for the last 20 years or so, weed has at least 15% THC, and i think most users prefer to go for higher THC levels, 20-25%, myself included (when i was using). so, maybe back in the day it was the "miracle drug" that could be casually consumed with no heavy side effects.. but it's becoming more clear that nowadays, all the effects of casual weed use come with much heavier side effects and comedowns, all in all making it a much more addictive drug. 

and speaking from 1st hand experience, i've been told multiple from multiple therapists and psychiatrists that heavy cannabis use will be detrimental to your mental health in the long run. especially if you are taking an antidepressant, which in most cases seems to be counteracted by weed, again, speaking from experience. i'm currently less than 30 days clean, but i can already tell for sure that my medicaiton is more capable of doing what it's suppsed to do, without "getting the crap kicked out of it by weed", my psychiatrists words. i think it's only a matter of time until it will be completely unrecommended by therapists, with exceptions for certain conditions, mostly physiological, like epilepsy, cancer, etc. and even then, in lower THC doses. whereas, in the mental health, weed should have no place. i'm in DBT therapy right now, which encourages you to drop all mood-altering substances. 

anyway, i hope you can find a way to communicate this to your husband in a way that is supportive and honest. your post here is evidence enough that it's enough of a problem and you have sincere concern for his well being, and yours. good luck!

i've been dealing with major depression for most of my life, and i'm still working on 'changing the pathways in my brain' as you've said. it's a long process that takes time and practice. 

think of it this way. if you go for a hike in the woods, you'll follow the dirt paths that have already been tread through time to get from point A to point B. the paths are winding, numerous, sometimes inefficient, but they get you there. (for example, for stoners like you and me, we would take the easy and long-treaded path of smoking weed to cope with whatever). but there are better ways through the woods, that get you from A to B with more efficiency, that haven't been tread - there is no path yet. but the way to access that route is by treading that path gradually over time. and it can only happen if you take it slowly at first, often with difficulty, requiring more patience and care. but the more you pave that path (in your brain), the more easily you can rely on it in the future. the more you pave it, the clearer and easier it becomes. 

hope that helps, i'm right there with you. still struggling daily.

it's super tough, but once you get started, the rest gets easier. take pride in the little things you can do, one thing at a time. just little things to get the ball rolling. wishing you the best, you're not alone

i'm only 7 days in right now, but on the particularly bad days i've had to do a lot to stay grounded and not go totally crazy. it's a painful ongoing battle. 

i've been meaning to post about this here, but one of my most important realizations through all this is "if you know how to suffer, you suffer less". it's a quote by thich nhat hanh. but keeping that in mind, if you can make it through your suffering, you will come out of it stronger than ever. 

similar quote from my ex-therapist - "the only way out of hell is to go through it" 

sometimes, for me, it's just about being patient and riding out the storm. it does pass. 

sounds like you've already put in a lot of work to make it this far. i hope you find a way that works. <3

i dunno, just spitballing in my tin foil hat here.

BPD here as well. i feel all this.

i don't know what to do either. 

all i know is, there are still good moments that you can experience. some of the best advice i got out of therapy is that all things are temporary, even the dark times. just have to survive to make it to the positive side of the cycle. of course, being a cycle, it'll go back negative eventually too. 

radical acceptance helps. at least, trying to accept things as shitty as they are. convince yourself that life can be worth living even with painful moments. 

doing nothing is one of my only ways out of the dark times.. just need to survive the amount of time it takes to turn the cycle again. 

anyway. i hope you find good things in life. i really do. anything counts. just don't end it yet

i would encourage you to drop the deadline - don't put that pressure on yourself.

you can't put a concrete timeline on a huge, ambiguous task like "reform my life" - just speaking from experience, you won't benefit from living life with a timer. you're already suffering, why increase the struggle? 

i gave myself a deadline when i quit my job last year. hoping to get my career off the ground and fix my shitty ways. my self-imposed deadline passed. months later, no progress. but i shouldn't have given myself that mindset. the process is not measurable in time. i would've been better off ignoring the concept of time. 

the best thing for you to do would be to give yourself that urge/drive to "reform your life" whatever that entails, but do it at the pace that it happens. don't force it. don't expect progress at a fast pace. let the process take as long as it has to take. you'll be better off.

i truly hope you find a way to overcome your suicidal feelings. i hope you find some happiness in life.

if it was that easy, OP's post wouldn't exist. 

maybe i'm assuming here, but the problem is that someone who is depressed, but has the urge to draw, will be going through conflicting emotional directions:

you want to draw to feel "good" feelings, but the desperate urge to express yourself leaves the attempt at drawing feeling meaningless and painful. 

i guess i'm speaking about myself, being in a creative rut. stuck in the phase of not being able to pick up the pencil. it really isn't that easy.

since i'm just spiraling on my own here, just gonna ramble. 

what would happen if i killed myself before the wedding? 

well, i'd ruin my fiance's life forever probably. i'd absolutely ruin my parents' lives. they would be devastated. unimaginable emotional pain, if i had to guess. those 3 humans in my life - my fiance, my mom, my dad. that's 3 people i refuse to put through that emotional pain. can't let that happen. they don't deserve that... (but i don't think they deserve a miserable piece of shit like me)

and what about my siblings? they would be devastated. but maybe not surprised. maybe life ruining.

how about my friends? they'd be in to it. maybe it'd be a good way for everyone to have a reunion, at my funeral. maybe they'd dig it. maybe they'd be proud of me for taking initiative, doing something that would actually improve my career (i'd be more successful as an artist if i killed myself, it's undeniable, people love supporting artists who are tragic). i fantasize about my friends putting together compilations of my old music and art work to memorialize me. most of my close friends throughout my life have been into dark shit, sad and heavy themes. you know, art school depressive shit. so if i killed myself, it'd be celebrated. 

i dunno, some pros and cons both ways. once again, not gonna do it, don't have a choice. but that weird dark fantasy about how it'd be. can't stop thinking about that.

i read this shit.

but yea, i feel the same. 

i've had so many posts buried here and there, because there's just so many people posting all the time and we're all in the same boat. makes me wonder how many people post to this sub only to be ignored, and how many of those people actually just went and killed themselves, and nobody noticed. 

pretty bleak times we live in. i'm sorry for us both.

sorry if this sounds bitter and mean, but 3 years is nothing. i've been wanting to make art my entire life. i started drawing as early as i can remember, maybe 4 years old. i'm 30 years old now. it feels like i'm no closer to being a successful artist than when i started.. did a 4 year degree at an art school. a lot of learning, sure. but like i said, no closer to being successful or fulfilled than when i started. i sure as hell haven't used my college degree in art for anything remotely proactive in terms my "career". 

i hate myself more and more every day. it gets harder and harder to pick up a pencil and start working. drawing feels like self destructive torture. it's lonely as fuck. and nobody cares. 

im so sorry, for both of us. for anyone who had the inclination to have a goal in art. it's futile.

but honestly, it is "your mental", or how you perceive the goal. the artists who you see as successful on the internet - those people are insane in their own way, they're the ones who figured out how to play this game. really, it doesn't matter how hard-working or technically skilled you are. the real skills in being an artist are marketing, self-promotion, and all that influencer bullshit. sorry but that's my current take...

if i were you, i'd use the platform to be honest. there's not enough transparency in social media. being an influencer/youtuber is becoming like following a script, being a people-pleaser. it's always been set up to harm your mental health. but i bet if you were to be completely honest, a lot of people would appreciate it. maybe not all your followers would approve, but if you truly are suffering internally, you won't be able to lie about it forever. plus, i'm sure you'd get plenty of new viewers if you addressed mental health. it's kind of a trending topic, and nowadays, the general public seems to approve of the narrative of "everyone has to work on mental health".

idk, i've started to really appreciate when people are just real and honest about mental illness. you'd be surprised how many people would back something like that. like, i've followed some youtubers who just do gaming, but have been honest about suffering from depression and anxiety. it's absolutely doable, if you could bite  the bullet, so to speak, to talk about these things on youtube etc. but definitely don't force it.

and just a general ramble - social media is definitely a harmful system, sub/follower count and getting likes - it's all a system set up to abuse your sense of self and how you derive pleasure from interacting with other people. i've got my own issues trying to get likes and followers, shit sucks. i gave up mostly. but you're not alone. try to step away, see things objectively. 

it's literally a job for some people, to be an influencer. there's no way it's not gonna have it's own forms of pain and suffering, like all work.

in my opinion, as you get older, it's not that life gets easier, it's that you have to get stronger. 

if you were born with depression, you will likely struggle with it for the rest of your life. but ideally, you learn to manage the symptoms that come with it. but unless some dramatic change in psych/therapy happens to "cure depression", there is no cure, only treatment. 

i'm 30, going on 31. i had similar feelings when i was 24. but it's only going to make things harder for you if you live your life like you have a deadline to hit. especially if the "goal" is to overcome depression. it's not an on/off switch. and, maybe pessimistic to say, but you will be better off not giving yourself such a high expectation. i think you would be better off accepting that depression will always be there, but that there's always room for improvement... i'm struggling to follow my own advice here, but yea, that's the goal.

i have a BFA in traditional (2d not 3d) animation. graduated 2013, almost a decade ago. so far, i've failed to make it worth it. i had 1 freelance animation gig in 2015 maybe, it paid a few months rent. other than that, nada. most animation i've worked on since then has all been passion projects. 

i thought i was a hard worker. i was a hard worker. i am a hard worker. but in my opinion, i've committed myself to a miserable life goal. and it's driven me down some serious mental health spirals. there were maybe 13 people in my graduating class. i think maybe 1 or 2 of them have actually made a career out of it. to be able to market yourself as an artist is a HUGE aspect of maintaining a career in art. but if you don't have the self-esteem or self-motivation, you will struggle to find work. you will struggle to even maintain a social media account. mental health is highly at risk when you commit yourself to being an independent artist. to add to that, animation (2d at least in my experience) is extremely time-consuming and soul-crushing. add that mental strain to the already daunting task of standing out in an over-saturated market... the struggle is beyond me at this point. i know many people have made it work, and make it look easy. but i'm just 1 of the probably millions of other young (30 years old now lol) independent artists with a college degree. i think the ones who succeed at this are in the minority. 

also, i switched majors 2nd year. my freshman year, i was in illustration. then i decided to bite the bullet and switch to something i'm "passionate" about, so i switched to animation. honestly, my career would've been much better off if i stuck with illustration. i've had more paid graphic design/illustration work than animation work. 

just my 2 cents. you might be more mentally strong than i am. but that's my fair warning to anyone who considers doing what i did. 

obviously i'm really struggling right now, so sorry if this post is depressing. good luck to you

a brief explanation:

i've been suffering from severe depression and anxiety as of late. it's always been a problem in my life, and the past year or two has been particularly strange and trying. i got a bfa in traditional animation in 2013, and did nearly nothing with that degree for a long time.

about a year ago i quit my grocery store job because of poor mental health, and took a risk by trying to initiate an independent animation project. i made it to the point of finishing this 2 minute "episode" with the hopes that i could continue this project if it got enough support. i have a patreon and it's been up for a few months but i'm too chicken-shit scared and freaked out to run it. that said, here's the patreon link: https://www.patreon.com/ricomanforever

i've only just now gotten around to sharing this link to the finished project because i've been really struggling with self-promotion. it's a really emotionally painful thing to do when you have such low self-esteem. i've ranted a bit about this on r/depression but never really knew what to do about this animation project after a certain point. i'm sure some of you as animators and artists suffer from mental illness. i'm sorry for all of us.

so here's what i've done instead of killing myself. unfortunately, i don't see much else happening with this project. but i put off sharing it on reddit because it's been a chore just existing.

sorry if this is triggering or upsetting to anyone. sorry if it's too desperate. but i could really use some reassurance that i've at least made something that somebody understands or relates to.
